_about: Phase 7b teaching model of joints and ligaments. Shapes and attachments come from Z-Anatomy (ligaments) and BodyParts3D (bones). Each ligament is a set of straight fibres (tethers) between its two attachments: slack up to the toe strain, then taut (it holds). Joints keep their cartilage surfaces from passing through each other and are pressed gently closed. No forces in newtons: the numbers below are teaching values unless a source is given.

toe_strain.note: A fibre is slack until it is this much longer than at rest (the 'toe region' of a ligament), then it holds.

tear_strain.note: With 'ligaments can tear' on, a fibre this much longer than at rest tears, and with it the whole ligament part. Measured ultimate elongation of each ankle ligament is in Siegler 1988 (PMID 3366428); that paper was not read, so it is not used.

sources.ref: Siegler S, Block J, Schneck CD. Foot Ankle 1988;8(5):234-42
sources.claim: ultimate load of the lateral ligaments rises front to back; posterior tibiotalar highest of the medial

sources.ref: Attarian DE et al. Foot Ankle 1985;6(2):54-8
sources.claim: anterior talofibular lowest load to failure, deep deltoid highest

strength_order.use: shown as information only; every ligament has the same teaching values

solver._about: Quasi-static position-based solver (no forces in newtons). Ligament fibres and joint surfaces are hard limits; the 'seat' (soft tissue and muscle tone holding a bone in place) and the examiner's push are soft.

Fibula.r.why: the proximal tibiofibular joint is outside these regions' data: the top of the fibula is held in place

solver._compliance: Softness of a soft link: the larger, the softer (a bone's own weight is about 1-3). Ligament fibres and joint surfaces have 0 (hard).

stress_tests.name: Anterior drawer
stress_tests.limits: Abnormal: 10 mm or more, or 3 mm or more than the other side (most common thresholds in the literature).

sources.ref: Guerra-Pinto F et al. J Foot Ankle Surg 2021;60(6):1241-53 (systematic review)
Chang SH et al. J Am Acad Orthop Surg 2021;29(1):3-16
sources.claim: examine the drawer in about 16 degrees of plantar flexion (not modelled: the foot stays in its rest position)

stress_tests.pivot_note: Talar tilt hinges at the medial edge of the talar dome; external rotation turns about the centre of the dome (axis along the tibia); the drawer moves the whole foot forward.

stress_tests.name: Talar tilt (inversion)
stress_tests.limits: Abnormal: 10 degrees or more, or 6 degrees or more than the other side (most common thresholds).

sources.ref: Guerra-Pinto F et al. J Foot Ankle Surg 2021;60(6):1241-53 (systematic review)
Frost SC, Amendola A. Clin J Sport Med 1999;9(1):40-5
sources.claim: normal and injured values overlap widely

stress_tests.pivot_note: Talar tilt hinges at the medial edge of the talar dome; external rotation turns about the centre of the dome (axis along the tibia); the drawer moves the whole foot forward.

stress_tests.name: External rotation stress
stress_tests.limits: Medial clear space on a stress view: 5 mm or more suggests a deep deltoid tear (6 mm: no false positives in a cadaver study). Tibiofibular clear space: under about 6 mm is normal.

sources.ref: Ashraf A et al. J Orthop Trauma 2017;31(5):270-4 (gravity stress, cadavers)
Harper MC, Keller TS. Foot Ankle 1989;10(3):156-60

readouts.medial_gap: Medial gutter gap, talus to medial malleolus (mm)
readouts.lateral_gap: Ankle joint gap, lateral half of the dome (mm)
readouts._note: Gaps are bone surface to bone surface on these meshes (cartilage is part of the bone surface), so they are not X-ray clear spaces; the value at rest is shown next to each.

tether_bones._about: Only where the bones found automatically (the two bones the Z-Anatomy mesh touches most) disagree with the ligament's own name. A pair applies to every part; 'parts' gives one pair per part (parts ordered from patient right/lateral to left/medial); 'fan_from' makes one tether from that bone to every other bone the mesh touches.

z_anatomy_notes: Tibionavicular ligament: the Z-Anatomy mesh ends on the talus (no point within 6 mm of the navicular), so its tether runs tibia - talus. Not changed (no hand-made anatomy).

Cuneometatarsal interosseous ligaments: three small parts, medial cuneiform - 1st metatarsal, intermediate - 2nd, lateral - 3rd. There is no medial cuneiform - 2nd metatarsal (Lisfranc) ligament in Z-Anatomy.

Long plantar ligament: one sheet that touches the calcaneus, all five metatarsals and the medial cuneiform (cuboid 1.6 mm away); modelled as a fan of tethers from the calcaneus to every bone it touches.
Intersesamoid ligament: both sesamoids are one mesh in the sources, so it joins nothing (shown only).
